The React Compiler can be told what the exports of a module are, for example which of them are hooks. It reports here when that description contradicts itself, such as a hook with a name that does not start with `use`.

`bun lint` runs the compiler's checks with a fixed configuration that is valid, so this rule has nothing to report. It exists because the `recommended` config of `eslint-plugin-react-hooks` turns it on, and an ESLint config that does so has to keep working.

{/* never reports */}

## Examples

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```jsx
import { useForm } from "react-hook-form";

function SignUp() {
  const { register } = useForm();
  return <input {...register("email")} />;
}
```
